data.title: Ethereum Reclaims $2,600 as Average Transaction Fee Falls to $0.095
data.description: Ethereum rose to reclaim $2,600 on Friday as its average transaction fee fell to $0.095, down from a 2026 peak of $0.72. According to NS3.AI, analyst Ali Martinez said a strong four-hour close above $2,570, supported by volume, could open a path toward $2,700 and potentially $3,000. Santiment cautioned that lower fees alone do not indicate stronger demand.

data.title: Nscale Files To Go Public On NYSE Under Ticker NSCL
data.description: According to CNBC, Nscale, a cloud provider focused on infrastructure for artificial intelligence models, has filed to go public on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "NSCL." In its IPO prospectus, the London-based company reported a $1.02 billion net loss on $140.6 million in revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with a $368.9 million net loss and $10.4 million in revenue a year earlier. Nscale said its customers include OpenAI, Anthropic and Microsoft, and that it rents Nvidia graphics processing units for training and running models. The company also said it plans to acquire Anyscale, named Fidji Simo to its board last week, and had more than 1,000 full-time employees as of Aug. 31, 2026.

data.title: JP Morgan Struggles to Forecast Oil Prices Amid US-Iran War
data.description:
JP Morgan said it cannot reliably model the economic endgame of the US-Iran war, as oil prices, inflation and borrowing costs have moved beyond the bank’s earlier assumptions, according to BBC. The investment bank had expected a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in June and said its red lines included oil above $100 a barrel, US inflation at 4%, gasoline above $5 a gallon and 10-year government borrowing costs at 5%.

In the note, JP Morgan said many of those thresholds have now been crossed, but the exit strategy is less clear. It estimated oil’s fair value for September at about $90 a barrel even though it has traded above $100 in recent weeks, and said the market is pricing in the risk of further disruption to trade. Analysts also pointed to risks in the Bab al-Mandab Strait and said there are no clear signs of de-escalation.

data.title: Former FTC Technologist Warns Government AI Antitrust Exemptions Could Create a Cartel
data.description:
Neil Chilson, head of AI policy at the Abundance Institute and former FTC chief technologist, warned that government-backed antitrust exemptions for frontier AI labs could create a durable "cartel," according to Bloomberg.

He said companies can coordinate on safety standards without suspending antitrust rules and that existing consumer-protection and liability laws already provide tools to address harms caused by AI.

data.title: Crusoe Raises Nearly $4 Billion, Valuation Nears $31 Billion
data.description:
Crusoe CEO Chase Lochmiller said the AI infrastructure company raised nearly $4 billion in fresh funding, lifting its valuation to almost $31 billion, according to Bloomberg.

He said the capital will support Crusoe’s push to build AI infrastructure across data centers, cloud computing and managed AI services. Lochmiller also said Crusoe could eventually enter public markets and argued the data center industry has a “marketing issue” and needs to better communicate its impact on water, jobs and local tax revenue.

data.title: US Dollar Flat as Yen Narrows Losses After BOJ Rate Check Reports
data.description:
The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index was little changed at 1,203.15 on Friday, and the dollar was still headed for its best weekly performance since June. According to Sina Finance, the yen narrowed its losses after reports that the Bank of Japan had sounded out market participants on exchange rates.

Dollar/yen rose 0.5% to 156.75. The yen had fallen sharply earlier after the Bank of Japan raised interest rates as expected but gave no clear guidance on whether borrowing costs would be increased further.

Geoffrey Yu, senior strategist at BNY Mellon, said the market may think the Bank of Japan was not hawkish enough, which helped drive the rebound in dollar/yen. He added that investors will watch whether officials signal to the market to defend the effectiveness and credibility of recent foreign-exchange action.

The yen was the worst-performing G10 currency against the dollar on Friday and for the week. Sterling rose 0.2% to 1.3389 against the dollar, while the euro gained 0.1% to 1.1483.

A gauge of French government bond risk rose 1 percentage point, reflecting growing investor caution amid France's large budget deficit and continued political uncertainty.

data.title: AI | Anthropic's Existential Risk Warnings Dominate Broader AI Debate
data.description:
Anthropic's warnings about losing control of AI are drawing more attention as AI begins helping build the next generation of AI, according to Bloomberg.

Critics say the focus on existential risk is overshadowing problems already here. Bloomberg's Rachel Metz and Davey Alba discussed the reporting with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech."

The options all expire on October 2, and a regulatory filing due in mid-November could provide more information about his holdings.

data.title: Elon Musk Urges AI Model Testing Before Release Amid Safety Debate
data.description: According to CNBC, Elon Musk said companies should test one another’s new AI models for safety issues before release, arguing that this approach is preferable to heavy government regulation. Speaking virtually at the All-In Summit on Tuesday, Musk said regulatory oversight is difficult to roll back once expanded. The article said Musk’s comments came after he agreed with Dario Amodei and Sam Altman on slowing foundation model development, while President Donald Trump and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued AI firms should move faster. CNBC also reported that Musk has recently backed calls for caution even as his businesses remain deeply tied to AI, including SpaceX’s merger with xAI in February and a $60 billion acquisition of AI coding tools provider Cursor in August.
